headline: High-risk filesystem overlap and default data-flow coupling create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem; ms-swift also reads/writes files and processes logs/configs. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other’s outputs from shared files. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF ms-swift ingests files produced by Mentat as prompts or configs
IF Mentat treats file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Add a manual review step before either agent reads the other's outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared reference data
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on exchanged files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and sends context to a configured model provider; ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and hub/sdk tokens. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or training artifacts can flow into either agent’s outbound API calls, creating exfiltration risk in default use. The pair’s overlap is broader than a small local-only leak.
conditions: IF the same directory contains source code and training artifacts
IF either agent forwards file contents to its backend or external API
IF secrets are present in logs, configs, checkpoints, or code
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Use separate API credentials per agent
Restrict each agent to least-privilege file subsets
Redact logs and configs before either agent reads them
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound file uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can modify git state and write the filesystem; ms-swift can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. On a shared directory, both can mutate the same artifacts without documented locking, so concurrent edits or environment changes can corrupt state or overwrite each other.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or output directory
IF ms-swift installs packages or runs shell commands in that environment
IF Mentat applies diffs while ms-swift is mutating files
mitigations: Run agents in separate directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable package installation in shared environments
Commit or snapshot state before handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and ms-swift can act as a CLI/Python workflow over files, logs, and outputs. If ms-swift consumes Mentat’s outputs without verification, an error in one agent can propagate into downstream actions or training/evaluation artifacts. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show automatic action-taking by default.
conditions: IF ms-swift uses Mentat-generated diffs or text as authoritative input
IF no human or validator checks the intermediate output
IF downstream scripts or evaluations are run on the resulting files
mitigations: Require a human review of Mentat diffs
Validate outputs against schema or tests before reuse
Keep generated artifacts separate from source inputs
Add checksum checks between handoffs
requires-engineering: insert a verification gate between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat is documented as handling source code and model-provider API keys, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and hub/sdk tokens. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, so a specific breach cannot be proven; however, the mixed data classes and external API usage create a plausible retention/logging mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent’s workspace
IF logs or checkpoints retain that data beyond policy
IF one agent’s backend stores prompts or files longer than the other’s policy allows
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review retention settings before execution
Separate credentials and storage buckets
Delete transient logs after each run
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
